@@ -0,0 +1,337 @@
+# hitbut — requirements
+
+What hitbut must do, leaf by leaf. Every numbered leaf below is claimed by exactly one
+executable case, of the kind that can actually observe what the leaf asserts; the coverage
+gate fails if that stops being true. The mechanism behind these requirements — what runs
+where and why — is [`docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`](../../docs/architecture/DESIGN.md); this
+document is what the product must *do*, and the harness that runs it is
+[`dev/requirements/README.md`](README.md).
+
+> **Green here means "claimed by a passing case", not "verified in the world".** The
+> server- and screen-kind cases run the shipped Worker on the real `workerd` runtime, but
+> against local D1, R2 and Queues — they confirm our code *asks* Cloudflare for the right
+> thing, not that Cloudflare performs it. That gap, and four others (the judge model is
+> unevaluated for Hebrew, there is no real-source matrix yet, requirement `7.1` is
+> provisional, the legal review is outstanding), are tracked in
+> [#28](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/28).
+
+**Scope of v1.** Israeli politicians, journalists and commentators; statements mostly in
+Hebrew, some in English. The corpus is the product — a figure's record, checkable in one
+place with the evidence attached — and inconsistency detection is one lens over it.
+
+**A note on the sample data.** Every figure, quote, date and count in the fixtures and in
+the committed screenshots is fictional. Nothing in this repository attributes a statement
+to a real person.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Corpus and identifiers
+
+Researchers and journalists cite these ids, so an id is a promise: it is never reused,
+renumbered, or deleted, and retirement is a status rather than a removal.
+
+- `1.1` A figure's id is a slug minted once at creation, and does not change when the figure's display name changes.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The slug is derived from the name at creation — Hebrew stays Hebrew, since transliterating
+  without vowels is a guess and a guess baked into a permanent id is a guess forever;
+  collisions take a numeric suffix. From then on the id is opaque: renaming מורג to
+  מורג־עציון updates `display_name` and leaves `id` alone, because a citation of the old URL
+  must keep resolving.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.2` A statement keeps the ULID it was given at first extraction when the same source payload is extracted again.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Re-extraction happens whenever a parser is fixed and replayed over the R2 payload cache.
+  Identity is `(source id, the statement's position in that payload)`; a second run over the
+  same bytes must produce the same ids, or every citation breaks on every parser fix.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.3` A statement whose source does not establish a date stores no date — not today's, not the epoch, not the fetch time.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Unknown is a state of its own. The column is nullable, the API omits the key rather than
+  sending a default, and the site renders "תאריך לא ידוע" — three stages, one meaning. A
+  defaulted date would silently order a timeline wrongly and look entirely plausible.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.4` A figure withdrawn from the product is marked retired and still resolves by id.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Withdrawal is an editorial act (a misattribution, a person out of scope). The row stays,
+  `status` becomes `retired`, listings exclude it, and a direct fetch by id still answers —
+  with the status — so an old citation degrades to "this record was withdrawn" rather than
+  to a 404.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.5` Re-analysis of a statement pair writes a new inconsistency record and marks the previous one superseded, never overwriting it.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A prompt or model change re-judges pairs. The old record keeps its id, gains
+  `superseded_by`, and drops out of the surfaced set; the new record is the live one. A
+  reader who cited the old judgment can still see exactly what was said and what replaced it.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.6` Two statements minted in the same millisecond get distinct ids that still sort in mint order.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A single payload yields many statements at once. ULID monotonicity within a millisecond
+  is what keeps "the order they were extracted in" recoverable from the ids alone.
+  </details>
+
+## 2. Hebrew-aware search
+
+SQLite's FTS tokenizers split Hebrew on whitespace and nothing else, so `בכנסת` and `כנסת`
+are unrelated words to them. Hebrew glues its prepositions, articles and conjunctions onto
+the front of the word, so an unaided index answers "no results" for most of the ways a
+person actually types. hitbut folds the text itself, on both sides of the query.
+
+- `2.1` A search for a Hebrew word matches statements where that word carries an attached prefix.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Querying `כנסת` matches text containing `בכנסת`, `לכנסת`, `שבכנסת`. The indexer emits both
+  the surface token and its stripped stem; the query does the same, so the match happens in
+  the index rather than in a `LIKE` scan.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.2` A word written with a final-form letter matches the same word written without it, and the reverse.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  ם/מ, ן/נ, ך/כ, ף/פ, ץ/צ. Stripping a prefix exposes this constantly: `מהם` stripped to
+  `הם` must still meet `הם` indexed elsewhere, and quoted transcripts are inconsistent about
+  final forms mid-word.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.3` Niqqud, geresh and gershayim are folded away before indexing and before matching.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  `ח״כ` and `חכ` are the same query; a vocalised quote from a formal transcript must meet an
+  unvocalised one from a press release.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.4` A Latin-script query matches Latin statement text and is not touched by the Hebrew folding.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Not every statement in scope is Hebrew. `budget` must not be stemmed by rules meant for
+  Hebrew prefixes, and a mixed-script statement is indexed under both scripts.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.5` A prefix is never stripped down to a stem too short to be a word.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  `בית` must not be indexed as `ית`, and `של` must not become `ל`. The floor is a
+  three-letter surface form; below it the surface token is the only thing indexed. Without
+  the floor, common short words match nearly everything.
+  </details>
+
+## 3. Acquisition
+
+Sources are other organisations' websites, reached without a contract: no changelog, no
+SLA, no support channel. Every leaf here exists to make a source's failure legible instead
+of turning it into corrupt data.
+
+- `3.1` The raw payload is written to the cache before anything parses it.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Ordering, not merely presence: the R2 write happens before the extractor is called, so a
+  payload that crashes the parser is still on disk to debug against and to replay.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.2` A fetch retries only the statuses another attempt could improve, and fails a client error on the first attempt.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 are worth another attempt with backoff. Any other 4xx is
+  about our request and will answer identically forever; retrying it wastes the budget and
+  looks like traffic worth blocking.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.3` A response whose body carries a bot-wall marker is recorded as blocked, never as content.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  An anti-bot interstitial arrives as a perfectly ordinary 200. Caching it stores a
+  challenge page that looks like data; the marker scan makes it a distinct, reportable
+  failure reason for that source.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.4` An empty body is a failure of that fetch, and is not retried.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Nothing rendered. A successful-but-empty response will keep being successful and empty, so
+  the retry budget buys nothing.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.5` One item failing in a batch is recorded with its reason and the rest of the batch still lands.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A run over a day of protocols must not lose the day because one document 404s. The run
+  reports per-item reasons and exits successfully — a declined item is a signal for a human,
+  not a broken pipeline.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.6` A re-run fetches only what is missing, unless a refresh is forced.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Resumability measured against the cache: a second pass over the same window issues no
+  requests. `force` re-fetches deliberately, which is the only way a changed upstream page
+  is re-read.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.7` A source module that does not declare its data surface and its refresh clock is refused by the registry.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The surface (`hydration` | `api` | `markup`) records which reconnaissance answer this
+  parser rests on; the clock records how fast that source actually moves. Both are required
+  at registration, so neither can be left to a comment.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.8` Extraction replays from the cached payload without touching the network.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A parser fix costs zero requests. The case runs extraction with the fetcher wired to throw
+  on any call, so a network read is a test failure rather than a slow test.
+  </details>
+
+## 4. Analysis
+
+Detection has to be defensible before it is clever: for every flag, a reader can see which
+two statements were compared, what was said about them, and by which model and prompt.
+
+- `4.1` Candidate pairs are drawn only from one figure's own statements, and only where the topics overlap.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Two figures disagreeing is not an inconsistency, and one figure's unrelated statements are
+  not a pair worth a model call. Pairing is the cost control and the correctness rule at once.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.2` A pair the judge calls contradictory is stored as kind `contradiction`.
+- `4.3` A pair the judge calls a change of position over time is stored as kind `position-shift`.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Distinct on purpose: a politician who changed their mind and said so is a different claim
+  about them than one who denies ever holding the position. The site labels them differently.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.4` A pair the judge calls consistent is stored with its score and never surfaced.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Keeping the negatives is what makes the threshold tunable later, and what stops the same
+  pair being paid for twice.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.5` Every stored judgment carries both statement ids, the rationale, and the model and prompt version that produced it.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The defensible trail. A prompt is a committed, versioned file; the version travels with

+# hitbut — requirements

+What hitbut must do, leaf by leaf. Every numbered leaf below is claimed by exactly one
+executable case, of the kind that can actually observe what the leaf asserts; the coverage
+gate fails if that stops being true. The mechanism behind these requirements — what runs
+where and why — is [`docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`](../../docs/architecture/DESIGN.md); this
+document is what the product must *do*, and the harness that runs it is
+[`dev/requirements/README.md`](README.md).
+
+> **Green here means "claimed by a passing case", not "verified in the world".** The
+> server- and screen-kind cases run the shipped Worker on the real `workerd` runtime, but
+> against local D1, R2 and Queues — they confirm our code *asks* Cloudflare for the right
+> thing, not that Cloudflare performs it. That gap, and four others (the judge model is
+> unevaluated for Hebrew, there is no real-source matrix yet, requirement `7.1` is
+> provisional, the legal review is outstanding), are tracked in
+> [#28](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/28).
+
+**Scope of v1.** Israeli politicians, journalists and commentators; statements mostly in
+Hebrew, some in English. The corpus is the product — a figure's record, checkable in one
+place with the evidence attached — and inconsistency detection is one lens over it.
+
+**A note on the sample data.** Every figure, quote, date and count in the fixtures and in
+the committed screenshots is fictional. Nothing in this repository attributes a statement
+to a real person.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Corpus and identifiers
+
+Researchers and journalists cite these ids, so an id is a promise: it is never reused,
+renumbered, or deleted, and retirement is a status rather than a removal.

+- `1.1` A figure's id is a slug minted once at creation, and does not change when the figure's display name changes.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The slug is derived from the name at creation — Hebrew stays Hebrew, since transliterating
+  without vowels is a guess and a guess baked into a permanent id is a guess forever;
+  collisions take a numeric suffix. From then on the id is opaque: renaming מורג to
+  מורג־עציון updates `display_name` and leaves `id` alone, because a citation of the old URL
+  must keep resolving.
+  </details>
+

+
+  Re-extraction happens whenever a parser is fixed and replayed over the R2 payload cache.
+  Identity is `(source id, the statement's position in that payload)`; a second run over the
+  same bytes must produce the same ids, or every citation breaks on every parser fix.
+  </details>

+  sending a default, and the site renders "תאריך לא ידוע" — three stages, one meaning. A

+to a real person.

+renumbered, or deleted, and retirement is a status rather than a removal.

+- `1.1` A figure's id is a slug minted once at creation, and does not change when the figure's display name changes.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The slug is derived from the name at creation — Hebrew stays Hebrew, since transliterating
+  without vowels is a guess and a guess baked into a permanent id is a guess forever;
+  collisions take a numeric suffix. From then on the id is opaque: renaming מורג to
+  מורג־עציון updates `display_name` and leaves `id` alone, because a citation of the old URL
+  must keep resolving.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.2` A statement keeps the ULID it was given at first extraction when the same source payload is extracted again.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Re-extraction happens whenever a parser is fixed and replayed over the R2 payload cache.
+  Identity is `(source id, the statement's position in that payload)`; a second run over the
+  same bytes must produce the same ids, or every citation breaks on every parser fix.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.3` A statement whose source does not establish a date stores no date — not today's, not the epoch, not the fetch time.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Unknown is a state of its own. The column is nullable, the API omits the key rather than
+  sending a default, and the site renders "תאריך לא ידוע" — three stages, one meaning. A
+  defaulted date would silently order a timeline wrongly and look entirely plausible.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.4` A figure withdrawn from the product is marked retired and still resolves by id.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Withdrawal is an editorial act (a misattribution, a person out of scope). The row stays,
+  `status` becomes `retired`, listings exclude it, and a direct fetch by id still answers —
+  with the status — so an old citation degrades to "this record was withdrawn" rather than
+  to a 404.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.5` Re-analysis of a statement pair writes a new inconsistency record and marks the previous one superseded, never overwriting it.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A prompt or model change re-judges pairs. The old record keeps its id, gains
+  `superseded_by`, and drops out of the surfaced set; the new record is the live one. A
+  reader who cited the old judgment can still see exactly what was said and what replaced it.
+  </details>
+
+- `1.6` Two statements minted in the same millisecond get distinct ids that still sort in mint order.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A single payload yields many statements at once. ULID monotonicity within a millisecond
+  is what keeps "the order they were extracted in" recoverable from the ids alone.
+  </details>
+
+## 2. Hebrew-aware search
+
+SQLite's FTS tokenizers split Hebrew on whitespace and nothing else, so `בכנסת` and `כנסת`
+are unrelated words to them. Hebrew glues its prepositions, articles and conjunctions onto
+the front of the word, so an unaided index answers "no results" for most of the ways a
+person actually types. hitbut folds the text itself, on both sides of the query.
+
+- `2.1` A search for a Hebrew word matches statements where that word carries an attached prefix.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Querying `כנסת` matches text containing `בכנסת`, `לכנסת`, `שבכנסת`. The indexer emits both
+  the surface token and its stripped stem; the query does the same, so the match happens in
+  the index rather than in a `LIKE` scan.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.2` A word written with a final-form letter matches the same word written without it, and the reverse.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  ם/מ, ן/נ, ך/כ, ף/פ, ץ/צ are positional variants of one letter. Sources disagree about
+  them — an acronym or a transliteration puts one mid-word, a hurried query types the other
+  — and treating them as different letters answers "no results" for a word the corpus
+  certainly contains. The fold runs on both sides, so `ירושלים` and `ירושלימ` are one term.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.3` Niqqud, geresh and gershayim are folded away before indexing and before matching.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  `ח״כ` and `חכ` are the same query; a vocalised quote from a formal transcript must meet an
+  unvocalised one from a press release.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.4` A Latin-script query matches Latin statement text and is not touched by the Hebrew folding.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Not every statement in scope is Hebrew. `budget` must not be stemmed by rules meant for
+  Hebrew prefixes, and a mixed-script statement is indexed under both scripts.
+  </details>
+
+- `2.5` A prefix is never stripped down to a stem too short to be a word.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  `בית` must not be indexed as `ית`, and `של` must not become `ל`. A strip that would leave
+  fewer than three letters is not made, so the surface token is the only thing indexed.
+  Without the floor, the commonest short words match nearly everything.
+  </details>

+## 3. Acquisition
+
+Sources are other organisations' websites, reached without a contract: no changelog, no
+SLA, no support channel. Every leaf here exists to make a source's failure legible instead
+of turning it into corrupt data.
+
+- `3.1` The raw payload is written to the cache before anything parses it.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Ordering, not merely presence: the R2 write happens before the extractor is called, so a
+  payload that crashes the parser is still on disk to debug against and to replay.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.2` A fetch retries only the statuses another attempt could improve, and fails a client error on the first attempt.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 are worth another attempt with backoff. Any other 4xx is
+  about our request and will answer identically forever; retrying it wastes the budget and
+  looks like traffic worth blocking.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.3` A response whose body carries a bot-wall marker is recorded as blocked, never as content.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  An anti-bot interstitial arrives as a perfectly ordinary 200. Caching it stores a
+  challenge page that looks like data; the marker scan makes it a distinct, reportable
+  failure reason for that source.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.4` An empty body is a failure of that fetch, and is not retried.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Nothing rendered. A successful-but-empty response will keep being successful and empty, so
+  the retry budget buys nothing.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.5` One item failing in a batch is recorded with its reason and the rest of the batch still lands.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A run over a day of protocols must not lose the day because one document 404s. The run
+  reports per-item reasons and exits successfully — a declined item is a signal for a human,
+  not a broken pipeline.
+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Resumability measured against the cache: a second pass over the same window issues no
+  requests. `force` re-fetches deliberately, which is the only way a changed upstream page
+  is re-read.
+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The surface (`hydration` | `api` | `markup`) records which reconnaissance answer this
+  parser rests on; the clock records how fast that source actually moves. Both are required
+  at registration, so neither can be left to a comment.
+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A parser fix costs zero requests. The case runs extraction with the fetcher wired to throw
+  on any call, so a network read is a test failure rather than a slow test.
+  </details>

+## 4. Analysis
+
+Detection has to be defensible before it is clever: for every flag, a reader can see which
+two statements were compared, what was said about them, and by which model and prompt.
+
+- `4.1` Candidate pairs are drawn only from one figure's own statements, and only where the topics overlap.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Two figures disagreeing is not an inconsistency, and one figure's unrelated statements are
+  not a pair worth a model call. Pairing is the cost control and the correctness rule at once.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.2` A pair the judge calls contradictory is stored as kind `contradiction`.
+- `4.3` A pair the judge calls a change of position over time is stored as kind `position-shift`.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Distinct on purpose: a politician who changed their mind and said so is a different claim
+  about them than one who denies ever holding the position. The site labels them differently.
+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+

+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+

+  every record it produced, so "which prompt said this?" is answerable years later.
+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Only high-confidence pairs reach the product; the full distribution stays for tuning.
+  Surfacing is a query, not a delete.
+  </details>

+- `5.3` `GET /api/v1/statements/{id}` returns the quote, its context, and the source it came from.
+- `5.4` `GET /api/v1/inconsistencies` returns surfaced records only, newest first.

+  A cited link to a superseded judgment answers 200 with the record and a pointer forward.
+  </details>
+

+  route actually runs it against the real index.
+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

+  implying it by routing failure.
+  </details>
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  An empty 200 for a missing entity turns a typo into "this person has said nothing",
+  which is the single most defamatory thing an empty page could imply here.
+  </details>

+## 6. The site
+
+RTL-first, Hebrew-primary, with the same layout mirrored for LTR content. Each leaf's
+expected result is the committed screenshot below it: approving the image is approving the
+page. The design system these render is the warm-editorial direction the owner approved on
+the design canvas.
+
+- `6.1` The home page leads with the search, then the most recent surfaced inconsistencies, then the tracked figures.
+<!-- gallery:6.1 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.1 -->
+
+- `6.2` A figure page shows the profile, the counts, the topics, and the statement timeline with flagged statements marked.
+<!-- gallery:6.2 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.2 -->
+
+- `6.3` A statement page shows the quote, its date, its context, and a link to the source it was taken from.
+<!-- gallery:6.3 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.3 -->
+
+- `6.4` An inconsistency page shows the two statements side by side, separated by the «אבל» mark, with the rationale and both sources.
+<!-- gallery:6.4 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.4 -->
+
+- `6.5` A search results page shows what matched, with the query's term highlighted in each result.
+<!-- gallery:6.5 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.5 -->
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>

+  compares two quotes we extracted from two sources, and says why it thinks they conflict —
+  it does not know what the person meant, and it can be wrong. Directly beside it: how to
+  tell us it is wrong.
+  </details>
+<!-- gallery:6.6 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.6 -->
+
+- `6.7` At phone width the inconsistency page stacks the two statements vertically with the mark between them.
+<!-- gallery:6.7 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.7 -->
+

+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Direction follows the content's language, not a site-wide setting: an English pair is a
+  left-to-right page in the same design system, which is what keeps non-Hebrew sources
+  inside v1 rather than deferred.
+  </details>
+<!-- gallery:6.8 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.8 -->

+
+- `7.1` A merge to `main` reaches the deployed site with no human build step. **[provisional — no case]**
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Listed in `dev/requirements/provisional.json`, which is the coverage gate's burn-down
+  list and currently holds this one entry. It cannot be asserted from a test: it is a claim
+  about a live account, and it burns down when phase 0 provisioning
+  ([#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27)) lands and a merge is observed end
+  to end.
+  </details>

+  The surface (`hydration` | `api` | `markup`) records which reconnaissance answer this
+  parser rests on; the clock records how fast that source actually moves. Both are required
+  at registration, so neither can be left to a comment.
+  </details>
+
+- `3.8` Extraction replays from the cached payload without touching the network.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  A parser fix costs zero requests. The case runs extraction with the fetcher wired to throw
+  on any call, so a network read is a test failure rather than a slow test.
+  </details>
+
+## 4. Analysis
+
+Detection has to be defensible before it is clever: for every flag, a reader can see which
+two statements were compared, what was said about them, and by which model and prompt.
+
+- `4.1` Candidate pairs are drawn only from one figure's own statements, and only where the topics overlap.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Two figures disagreeing is not an inconsistency, and one figure's unrelated statements are
+  not a pair worth a model call. Pairing is the cost control and the correctness rule at once.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.2` A pair the judge calls contradictory is stored as kind `contradiction`.
+- `4.3` A pair the judge calls a change of position over time is stored as kind `position-shift`.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Distinct on purpose: a politician who changed their mind and said so is a different claim
+  about them than one who denies ever holding the position. The site labels them differently.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.4` A pair the judge calls consistent is stored with its score and never surfaced.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Keeping the negatives is what makes the threshold tunable later, and what stops the same
+  pair being paid for twice.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.5` Every stored judgment carries both statement ids, the rationale, and the model and prompt version that produced it.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The defensible trail. A prompt is a committed, versioned file; the version travels with
+  every record it produced, so "which prompt said this?" is answerable years later.
+  </details>
+
+- `4.6` A judgment scoring below the surfacing threshold is retained and excluded from the surfaced set.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Only high-confidence pairs reach the product; the full distribution stays for tuning.
+  Surfacing is a query, not a delete.
+  </details>
+
+## 5. HTTP API
+
+Public, read-only JSON under `/api/v1`. The only writers are the cron trigger and the queue
+consumer; everything a reader sees comes through here, including the site's own pages.
+
+- `5.1` `GET /api/v1/figures` lists figures with a cursor, and that cursor returns the next page without repeats.
+- `5.2` `GET /api/v1/figures/{id}` returns the profile with its statement timeline, newest first.
+- `5.3` `GET /api/v1/statements/{id}` returns the quote, its context, and the source it came from.
+- `5.4` `GET /api/v1/inconsistencies` returns surfaced records only, newest first.
+- `5.5` `GET /api/v1/inconsistencies/{id}` resolves a superseded record and names what superseded it.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The other half of `1.5`: the invariant is only worth anything if the boundary honours it.
+  A cited link to a superseded judgment answers 200 with the record and a pointer forward.
+  </details>
+
+- `5.6` `GET /api/v1/search?q=` answers a Hebrew query whose term carries an attached prefix.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The boundary's half of `2.1`. The logic case proves the folding; this proves the deployed
+  route actually runs it against the real index.
+  </details>
+
+- `5.7` Every response carries open CORS headers.
+- `5.8` A write method is rejected with 405.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  There is no write surface to authenticate, so the boundary states that rather than
+  implying it by routing failure.
+  </details>
+
+- `5.9` An unknown path answers 404 with the JSON error envelope, not an HTML page.
+- `5.10` An unknown figure answers 404, never an empty 200.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  An empty 200 for a missing entity turns a typo into "this person has said nothing",
+  which is the single most defamatory thing an empty page could imply here.
+  </details>
+
+- `5.11` `GET /api/v1/export/statements.ndjson` serves the whole corpus as one JSON object per line.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  What a researcher reads instead of paginating the corpus: statement, speaker and source
+  per line, with the stable ids intact so a later pull can be diffed against this one. It
+  is a snapshot the scheduled run regenerates, not a query assembled per request — and
+  before the first run has written one, the route says exactly that rather than serving an
+  empty file that reads like an empty corpus.
+  </details>
+
+## 6. The site
+
+RTL-first, Hebrew-primary, with the same layout mirrored for LTR content. Each leaf's
+expected result is the committed screenshot below it: approving the image is approving the
+page. The design system these render is the warm-editorial direction the owner approved on
+the design canvas.
+
+- `6.1` The home page leads with the search, then the most recent surfaced inconsistencies, then the tracked figures.
+<!-- gallery:6.1 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.1 -->
+
+- `6.2` A figure page shows the profile, the counts, the topics, and the statement timeline with flagged statements marked.
+<!-- gallery:6.2 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.2 -->
+
+- `6.3` A statement page shows the quote, its date, its context, and a link to the source it was taken from.
+<!-- gallery:6.3 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.3 -->
+
+- `6.4` An inconsistency page shows the two statements side by side, separated by the «אבל» mark, with the rationale and both sources.
+<!-- gallery:6.4 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.4 -->
+
+- `6.5` A search results page shows what matched, with the query's term highlighted in each result.
+<!-- gallery:6.5 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.5 -->
+
+- `6.6` The methodology page states in plain Hebrew what detection confirms and what it does not, and how to report an error.
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  The honest-gap sentence, on the page a reader can reach from every flag: the model
+  compares two quotes we extracted from two sources, and says why it thinks they conflict —
+  it does not know what the person meant, and it can be wrong. Directly beside it: how to
+  tell us it is wrong.
+  </details>
+<!-- gallery:6.6 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.6 -->
+
+- `6.7` At phone width the inconsistency page stacks the two statements vertically with the mark between them.
+<!-- gallery:6.7 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.7 -->
+
+- `6.8` An English statement renders the whole page LTR, with the mark reading "but".
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Direction follows the content's language, not a site-wide setting: an English pair is a
+  left-to-right page in the same design system, which is what keeps non-Hebrew sources
+  inside v1 rather than deferred.
+  </details>
+<!-- gallery:6.8 -->
+<!-- /gallery:6.8 -->
+
+## 7. Shipping
+
+- `7.1` A merge to `main` reaches the deployed site with no human build step. **[provisional — no case]**
+  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
+
+  Listed in `dev/requirements/provisional.json`, which is the coverage gate's burn-down
+  list and currently holds this one entry. It cannot be asserted from a test: it is a claim
+  about a live account, and it burns down when phase 0 provisioning
+  ([#27](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/27)) lands and a merge is observed end
+  to end.
+  </details>

invariants making an id citable: slugs minted once, statement ids stable across
a re-extraction, unknown dates carried as null and omitted on the wire,
retirement as a status, and re-analysis superseding rather than overwriting.

could improve, treat an anti-bot interstitial as a refusal rather than as
content, write the payload to the raw cache before a parser sees it — and a
registry that refuses a source which has not declared its data surface and its
refresh clock. A parser fix then replays offline from the cache, and the
statements keep the ids anyone already cited.

Analysis pairs within one figure on shared topics, judges behind one interface
against a committed versioned prompt, and stores the full trail including the
negatives.

Proves 3.1-3.8 and 4.1-4.6.

content.subject: Author dev/requirements/requirements.md (phase 1 spec)
content.description: Numbered leaves for corpus, search, acquisition, analysis, API, site. Spec-only commit, no code alongside (feature-requirements-first).

content.subject: Build the executable-requirements harness + coverage gate
content.description: Kind registry (logic/behavior/server/screen), case discovery, bijection gate, per-kind runners, gallery generator + gate, CI wiring. Watch the gate go red first.

content.subject: Shared contract + corpus store (phases 2-3)
content.description: src/shared types, D1 schema+migrations, ULID/slug ids, Hebrew-aware search indexing, supersede-not-delete invariants, logic cases.

content.subject: Acquisition + analysis (phases 4-5)
content.description: Shared fetch module (retry/backoff/bot-wall/raw-to-R2), source registry, queue consumer, pairing, judge interface + versioned prompt, behavior cases.

content.subject: HTTP API on the real Worker (phase 6)
content.description: /api/v1 routes, cursor pagination, CORS, read-only, NDJSON export; server-kind cases against the real handler under miniflare/wrangler.

content.subject: Preact+Vite RTL frontend + screen goldens (phase 7)
content.description: Six pages against /api/v1, warm-editorial RTL-first design system, vendored fonts, Playwright goldens against a local preview of the real deployment.

content.subject: Deploy plumbing + phase 0 hand-over issue (phases 0, 8)
content.description: wrangler config, deploy workflow from main, and the human-only Cloudflare provisioning checklist issue.
content.activeForm: Wiring deploy and filing the provisioning issue

איך זה עובד

מאיפה מגיעות ההתבטאויות

ההתבטאויות נאספות ממקורות פומביים — פרוטוקולים, הודעות, פרסומים ושידורים. העמוד או הקובץ המקורי נשמר אצלנו כפי שהוא, לפני שתוכנה כלשהי מפרשת אותו, כך שאפשר לחזור אליו ולבדוק מה בדיוק נכתב שם. לכל התבטאות באתר יש קישור למקור שממנו נלקחה.

כשמקור לא מציין מתי נאמר משהו, לא נמציא תאריך: כתוב «תאריך לא ידוע», וההתבטאות ממוינת אחרי כל אלה שכן תוארכו.

מה בעצם מסומן

שתי התבטאויות של אותה דמות שנוגעות לאותו נושא נקראות יחד על ידי מודל שפה, שאומר אם הן מתנגשות («סתירה»), אם מדובר בשינוי עמדה לאורך זמן («שינוי עמדה»), או ששתיהן יכולות להתקיים יחד. כל סימון נשמר עם שני המזהים של ההתבטאויות, עם ההנמקה, ועם גרסת המודל וגרסת ההנחיה שהפיקו אותו — כדי שתמיד יהיה אפשר לראות מה בדיוק הושווה ולמה.

מה הסימון לא אומר

המודל משווה שני ציטוטים שחילצנו משני מקורות ואומר למה לדעתו הם מתנגשים. הוא לא יודע מה הדובר התכוון, הוא לא שומע נימה, הוא לא רואה הקשר שלא נכתב — והוא יכול לטעות. {' '} סימון הוא הזמנה לקרוא את שני הציטוטים ואת המקורות שלהם, לא מסקנה סופית. שני הציטוטים והמקורות מופיעים בעמוד הסימון בדיוק כדי שאפשר יהיה לבדוק אותו.

למצוא טעות ולדווח עליה

אם ציטוט שגוי, מיוחס לדמות הלא נכונה, נחתך באופן שמשנה את משמעותו, או שסימון פשוט לא נכון —{' '} אפשר לדווח כאן . כדאי לצרף את הקישור לעמוד ואת המזהה שמופיע בו.

מה קורה לקישורים ישנים

מזהה לא ממוחזר ולא נמחק. אם מודל חדש קורא מחדש צמד התבטאויות, הסימון הישן נשמר, מסומן כמי שהוחלף, ומפנה לחדש — כדי שהפניה שנעשתה אליו בעבר תמשיך לעבוד. דמות שהוסרה מהאתר נשארת נגישה לפי המזהה שלה, עם הערה שהרשומה הוסרה.

חיפוש בעברית

עברית מדביקה את מילות היחס לתחילת המילה, ומנוע החיפוש שמתחת לאתר לא יודע על כך דבר. לכן אנחנו מקפלים את הטקסט בעצמנו לפני האינדוקס וגם בזמן החיפוש: «בכנסת» ו«כנסת» הן אותה מילה, אותיות סופיות נחשבות זהות לרגילות, וניקוד וגרשיים מוסרים. המחיר הוא שלפעמים מילים שונות חולקות אותו גזע ומופיעות זו בתוצאות של זו.

); }

lines: + * The same two families as installable fonts, for the screen lane's font jail. The site
+ * loads woff2 through CSS, which fontconfig cannot read — and a Chromium with no readable
+ * font at all crashes its renderer, so the jail needs real files. Using our own families

1	# hitbut — requirements
2	
3	What hitbut must do, leaf by leaf. Every numbered leaf below is claimed by exactly one
4	executable case, of the kind that can actually observe what the leaf asserts; the coverage
5	gate fails if that stops being true. The mechanism behind these requirements — what runs
6	where and why — is [`docs/architecture/DESIGN.md`](../../docs/architecture/DESIGN.md); this
7	document is what the product must *do*, and the harness that runs it is
8	[`dev/requirements/README.md`](README.md).
9	
10	> **Green here means "claimed by a passing case", not "verified in the world".** The
11	> server- and screen-kind cases run the shipped Worker on the real `workerd` runtime, but
12	> against local D1, R2 and Queues — they confirm our code *asks* Cloudflare for the right
13	> thing, not that Cloudflare performs it. That gap, and four others (the judge model is
14	> unevaluated for Hebrew, there is no real-source matrix yet, requirement `7.1` is
15	> provisional, the legal review is outstanding), are tracked in
16	> [#28](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/28).
17	
18	**Scope of v1.** Israeli politicians, journalists and commentators; statements mostly in
19	Hebrew, some in English. The corpus is the product — a figure's record, checkable in one
20	place with the evidence attached — and inconsistency detection is one lens over it.
21	
22	**A note on the sample data.** Every figure, quote, date and count in the fixtures and in
23	the committed screenshots is fictional. Nothing in this repository attributes a statement
24	to a real person.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 1. Corpus and identifiers
29	
30	Researchers and journalists cite these ids, so an id is a promise: it is never reused,
31	renumbered, or deleted, and retirement is a status rather than a removal.
32	
33	- `1.1` A figure's id is a slug minted once at creation, and does not change when the figure's display name changes.
34	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
35	
36	  The slug is derived from the name at creation — Hebrew stays Hebrew, since transliterating
37	  without vowels is a guess and a guess baked into a permanent id is a guess forever;
38	  collisions take a numeric suffix. From then on the id is opaque: renaming מורג to
39	  מורג־עציון updates `display_name` and leaves `id` alone, because a citation of the old URL
40	  must keep resolving.
41	  </details>
42	
43	- `1.2` A statement keeps the ULID it was given at first extraction when the same source payload is extracted again.
44	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
45	
46	  Re-extraction happens whenever a parser is fixed and replayed over the R2 payload cache.
47	  Identity is `(source id, the statement's position in that payload)`; a second run over the
48	  same bytes must produce the same ids, or every citation breaks on every parser fix.
49	  </details>
50	
51	- `1.3` A statement whose source does not establish a date stores no date — not today's, not the epoch, not the fetch time.
52	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
53	
54	  Unknown is a state of its own. The column is nullable, the API omits the key rather than
55	  sending a default, and the site renders "תאריך לא ידוע" — three stages, one meaning. A
56	  defaulted date would silently order a timeline wrongly and look entirely plausible.
57	  </details>
58	
59	- `1.4` A figure withdrawn from the product is marked retired and still resolves by id.
60	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
61	
62	  Withdrawal is an editorial act (a misattribution, a person out of scope). The row stays,
63	  `status` becomes `retired`, listings exclude it, and a direct fetch by id still answers —
64	  with the status — so an old citation degrades to "this record was withdrawn" rather than
65	  to a 404.
66	  </details>
67	
68	- `1.5` Re-analysis of a statement pair writes a new inconsistency record and marks the previous one superseded, never overwriting it.
69	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
70	
71	  A prompt or model change re-judges pairs. The old record keeps its id, gains
72	  `superseded_by`, and drops out of the surfaced set; the new record is the live one. A
73	  reader who cited the old judgment can still see exactly what was said and what replaced it.
74	  </details>
75	
76	- `1.6` Two statements minted in the same millisecond get distinct ids that still sort in mint order.
77	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
78	
79	  A single payload yields many statements at once. ULID monotonicity within a millisecond
80	  is what keeps "the order they were extracted in" recoverable from the ids alone.
81	  </details>
82	
83	## 2. Hebrew-aware search
84	
85	SQLite's FTS tokenizers split Hebrew on whitespace and nothing else, so `בכנסת` and `כנסת`
86	are unrelated words to them. Hebrew glues its prepositions, articles and conjunctions onto
87	the front of the word, so an unaided index answers "no results" for most of the ways a
88	person actually types. hitbut folds the text itself, on both sides of the query.
89	
90	- `2.1` A search for a Hebrew word matches statements where that word carries an attached prefix.
91	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
92	
93	  Querying `כנסת` matches text containing `בכנסת`, `לכנסת`, `שבכנסת`. The indexer emits both
94	  the surface token and its stripped stem; the query does the same, so the match happens in
95	  the index rather than in a `LIKE` scan.
96	  </details>
97	
98	- `2.2` A word written with a final-form letter matches the same word written without it, and the reverse.
99	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
100	
101	  ם/מ, ן/נ, ך/כ, ף/פ, ץ/צ are positional variants of one letter. Sources disagree about
102	  them — an acronym or a transliteration puts one mid-word, a hurried query types the other
103	  — and treating them as different letters answers "no results" for a word the corpus
104	  certainly contains. The fold runs on both sides, so `ירושלים` and `ירושלימ` are one term.
105	  </details>
106	
107	- `2.3` Niqqud, geresh and gershayim are folded away before indexing and before matching.
108	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
109	
110	  `ח״כ` and `חכ` are the same query; a vocalised quote from a formal transcript must meet an
111	  unvocalised one from a press release.
112	  </details>
113	
114	- `2.4` A Latin-script query matches Latin statement text and is not touched by the Hebrew folding.
115	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
116	
117	  Not every statement in scope is Hebrew. `budget` must not be stemmed by rules meant for
118	  Hebrew prefixes, and a mixed-script statement is indexed under both scripts.
119	  </details>
120	
121	- `2.5` A prefix is never stripped down to a stem too short to be a word.
122	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
123	
124	  `בית` must not be indexed as `ית`, and `של` must not become `ל`. A strip that would leave
125	  fewer than three letters is not made, so the surface token is the only thing indexed.
126	  Without the floor, the commonest short words match nearly everything.
127	  </details>
128	
129	## 3. Acquisition
130	
131	Sources are other organisations' websites, reached without a contract: no changelog, no
132	SLA, no support channel. Every leaf here exists to make a source's failure legible instead
133	of turning it into corrupt data.
134	
135	- `3.1` The raw payload is written to the cache before anything parses it.
136	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
137	
138	  Ordering, not merely presence: the R2 write happens before the extractor is called, so a
139	  payload that crashes the parser is still on disk to debug against and to replay.
140	  </details>
141	
142	- `3.2` A fetch retries only the statuses another attempt could improve, and fails a client error on the first attempt.
143	  <details><summary>Detail</summary>
144	
145	  408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 are worth another attempt with backoff. Any other 4xx is
146	  about our request and will answer identically forever; retrying it wastes the budget and
147	  looks like traffic worth blocking.
148	  </details>
149	
150	- `3.3` A response whose body carries a bot-wall marker is recorded as blocked, never as content.

# The requirements harness

[`requirements.md`](requirements.md) is the spec. This is what runs it.

Every numbered leaf in the spec is claimed by exactly one case, in the folder of the kind
that can actually observe what the leaf asserts. The claim is the **file name**:
`<slug>.<leaf-id>.case.ts`. There is no registration step and no id inside the file — the
name is the whole of it, and [`coverage.test.ts`](coverage.test.ts) fails the build if the
correspondence breaks in either direction.

## The kinds

| Kind | What it can see | How a case runs |
|---|---|---|
| `logic` | a pure product rule | the shipped code, called directly |
| `behavior` | a driven action and its consequence | the shipped code over recording fakes |
| `server` | a rule the HTTP boundary enforces | the shipped Worker on `workerd`, from the committed `wrangler.toml` |
| `screen` | what a page looks like | the built site in a pinned Chromium, against a committed screenshot |

Adding a kind is a drop: declare it in [`registry.ts`](registry.ts), create
`<kind>/cases/` and `<kind>/run.test.ts`, and the gate, the runners and the gallery pick
it up with no edit to any of them.

## Running it

```sh
npm test              # logic + behavior + both gates — the inner loop, seconds
npm run test:server   # the real Worker; needs no Cloudflare account
npm run test:screen   # the browser lane; slowest, so it is its own lane
npm run test:all      # everything
```

## Changing what a page looks like

The committed PNG under a `screen` leaf is the **owner's approval record** of that page.
An agent may propose one for a brand-new leaf; nobody edits a committed one to make a
failing case pass.

  and decide whether the product or the expectation is wrong. If the answer is the
  expectation, that is the owner's call, made on the diff.

  rewrites the gallery in `requirements.md`, so the two cannot skew. The new images ride
  the pull request for review.

rendering is unstable the fix is the determinism — the pinned browser build, the font
jail, the fixed clock, the fakes — and not a threshold.

  differently; the lane refuses to run on any other, naming the one the goldens were made

  running Worker, both fulfilled at the browser; anything else is aborted, so a new
  external dependency breaks the run instead of quietly making it non-hermetic.
- **Fonts come from a jail.** One directory, holding the two families the site ships.
  Nothing installed on the machine can reach the page — one wider fallback glyph rewraps a
  line and moves every card below it.
- **Time and randomness are fixed**, at one reference instant shared with the fixtures.

## The sample corpus

[`shared/fixtures.ts`](shared/fixtures.ts) is the world every lane runs against. Every
figure, quote, date and publisher in it is invented, and the publishers say so — nothing
here attributes a statement to a real person, and a committed screenshot cannot be
mistaken for a record of anything real.

Preact and Vite, six pages, RTL-first with the whole design mirrored for

drawn, and Latin dates and quotes inside a Hebrew page had their parts
reordered without a bidi isolate.

requirements.md now embeds each approved rendering under its leaf, kept honest
by a gallery gate; \`npm run requirements:refresh\` regenerates images and
gallery together.

Proves 6.1-6.8.

Refs #25" && git log --oneline -1 && du -sh dev/requirements/screen/cases src/frontend/public/fonts dev/requirements/screen/fallback-fonts

> # hitbut's own build: the requirements suite, and the deploy that ships `main`.
name: product

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: product-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  checks:
    name: requirements (logic, behavior, server)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      # Watch the count, not the colour: a run that finds no tests exits green.
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run test:server
      # Phase 0's exit condition that needs no account: the committed wrangler.toml
      # builds and its bindings resolve.
      - run: npx wrangler deploy --dry-run --outdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/dry-run"

  screen:
    name: requirements (screen)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Pinned to the Playwright the goldens were rendered with. A different build
    # rasterises text differently, and the comparison would measure the renderer.
    container: mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.56.1-noble
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run test:screen
      - name: The pictures, when they disagree
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: screen-failures
          path: dev/requirements/failures/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  deploy:
    name: ship main
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    needs: [checks, screen]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
      CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - name: Is there an account to deploy to yet?
        id: account
        run: |
          if [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" ] || [ -z "$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID" ]; then
            echo "Cloudflare provisioning (issue #27) has not landed — nothing to deploy yet."
            echo "ready=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "ready=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - if: steps.account.outputs.ready == 'true'

**התבטאויות** — a sourced record of what Israeli public figures have said, each statement
kept with the document it came from, and, inside that record, the places where it does not
add up. The corpus is the product; inconsistency detection is one lens over it.

|---|---|

npm ci

npm run dev:api       # wrangler, locally
npm run dev:site      # vite, locally

input.title: Build hitbut v1: executable spec, corpus, acquisition, analysis, API and site
input.body:
Implements phases 1–8 of #25. The product runs end to end locally: a corpus with citable identifiers, acquisition that treats a source's failure as a failure, analysis behind one model interface, a read-only HTTP API on the real Worker, and the RTL-first site — with all 44 requirement leaves claimed by a passing case.

## What was built, and what it costs to check

**The spec is the backbone.** [`dev/requirements/requirements.md`](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/blob/claude/hitbut-product-setup-gre12m/dev/requirements/requirements.md) carries 44 numbered leaves. The coverage gate fails on a leaf with no case, a case claiming a leaf that does not exist, two cases claiming one leaf, a misnamed file, a kind folder no runner runs, an image in a coded kind, or a stray golden. It went red first — 43 unclaimed leaves — before a single case existed.

**Every leaf is proven by the kind that can see it.**

| Lane | Cases | What it runs |
|---|---|---|
| logic | 11 | the shipped code, called directly |
| behavior | 14 | the shipped code over recording fakes |
| server | 11 | the shipped Worker on `workerd`, from the committed `wrangler.toml` |
| screen | 8 | the built site in a pinned Chromium, byte-exact against committed screenshots |

`npm test` is 35 tests in about a second; the server and screen lanes are their own lanes. Every one is green, and the screen goldens are byte-identical on a second render.

**Three bugs were found by running the real thing rather than a model of it.** `btoa` refuses a Hebrew figure id, so every pagination cursor threw; a percent-encoded Hebrew id was never decoded before lookup, so every figure page 404'd; and the font jail exposed that our vendored subsets carry no `←` or `↗`, which were rendering as missing-glyph boxes. All three were invisible to the coded lanes.

## Two decisions worth your attention

**Hebrew slugs, not transliteration.** A figure's id is `אילנה-מורג-עציון`. Transliterating without vowels is a guess, and a guess baked into a permanent identifier is a guess forever.

**Search folds Hebrew on our side of the index.** D1 cannot load a tokenizer that understands the attached ב/ה/ו/ל/מ/ש, so the indexer emits each token plus its stems and the query does the same. It buys the recall — searching `כנסת` finds `בכנסת` and the reverse — and it costs precision, because some stems are shared by two different words. The methodology page says so in plain Hebrew.

## What this does not do

- **Nothing is deployed.** Phase 0 provisioning is human-only and is #27 — creating the D1 database, the R2 bucket, the queue, the Pages project and a scoped token. The deploy job exits clean and says so until those exist.
- **No real sources.** Acquisition's machinery is proven against a fixture source. Real ones need a `map-a-data-source` reconnaissance and your pick of the first two or three; inventing a sample would prove support for a target the world does not serve.
- **The judge is unevaluated for Hebrew.** The analysis cases run a scripted judge, so they prove the pipeline and say nothing about judgment quality.

Those, and what a local `workerd` cannot tell you about Cloudflare's, are written down in #28 and linked from a banner on the spec itself.

**Every figure, quote, date and publisher in the fixtures and the committed screenshots is invented**, and the publishers are named "לדוגמה" so a screenshot cannot be mistaken for a record of anything real.

## Folders this touched

```
dev/requirements/   the spec, the coverage and gallery gates, the four kind runners,
                    the sample corpus, and the 44 cases
dev/tools/          vendor-fonts.ts — downloads the site's fonts and writes the
                    @font-face rules; run by hand, output committed
src/shared/         the wire contract, and the Hebrew folding both halves need
src/backend/        one Worker: corpus (D1 schema + store), acquisition (one fetch
                    module + the source registry), analysis (pairing + the judge
                    interface + the versioned prompt), api (/api/v1 + NDJSON export)
src/frontend/       Preact + Vite: six pages, RTL-first with the same design mirrored
                    for English content, vendored fonts, a ~50-line router
.github/workflows/  product.yml — the lanes, the wrangler dry-run, and the deploy
docs/, README.md    the src READMEs now describe what is in them
```

Closes #25

input.body:
## Implemented (2026-08-21) — PR #29

Phases 1–8 are built and green; phase 0 is human-only and is now #27.

- **1. Harness** — `dev/requirements/` with four kinds (`logic`, `behavior`, `server`, `screen`), the bijection gate, per-kind runners, the gallery generator and its drift gate, wired into a `product` workflow. Watched red first: 43 unclaimed leaves.
- **2. Contract** — `src/shared/` carries the entities, the wire shapes and the Hebrew folding; the barrier holds.
- **3. Corpus** — D1 schema and store: slugs minted once (in Hebrew — transliteration without vowels is a permanent guess), statement ids stable across re-extraction, unknown dates null and omitted on the wire, retirement as status, supersede-never-overwrite.
- **4. Acquisition** — one fetch module (retry only what another attempt could improve, bot-wall detection, raw-to-cache before parse, batch isolation, offline replay) and a registry that refuses an undeclared source. **No real sources**: those need the recon and your pick.
- **5. Analysis** — queue consumer, same-figure/shared-topic pairing, judge behind one interface, committed versioned prompt, negatives retained, full trail on every record.
- **6. API** — `/api/v1` read-only with cursor pagination, open CORS, 405 on writes, superseded judgments still resolvable, and the NDJSON export the scheduled run writes to R2.
- **7. Site** — Preact + Vite, six pages, RTL-first with the same design mirrored for English content, vendored fonts, eight approved screenshots embedded in the spec.
- **8. Ship-on-green** — the deploy job applies migrations, ships the Worker and builds the site against the deployed API; it exits clean and says so until #27 lands.

**Decisions taken while building, worth knowing:**

1. **Hebrew figure slugs** rather than transliteration (`אילנה-מורג-עציון`).
2. **Search folds Hebrew on our side of the index** — recall bought at a precision cost, stated on the methodology page.
3. **The harness runs the committed `wrangler.toml` minus the `[ai]` binding**, derived at run time, because Workers AI has no local emulation and its presence makes wrangler demand an API token. Nothing in the server or screen lane goes near the judge.
4. **`5.11` was added to the spec** for the bulk NDJSON export, which phase 6 named but no leaf covered.

**Honest gaps** are #28, linked from a banner on the spec: the local platform is not Cloudflare's, the judge is unevaluated for Hebrew, there is no source matrix, `7.1` is provisional, and the Israeli defamation review is outstanding.

One more step, learned while wiring the deploy in #29 — add it to the checklist: - [ ] **Repository variable `API_ORIGIN`** = the deployed Worker's origin (e.g. `https://hitbut-api..workers.dev`, or the custom domain if you put one in front of it). Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → *Variables*, not Secrets.
*While off:* the site build fails loudly rather than shipping a site that fetches `/api/v1` from itself and shows nothing. The reason it is a build-time value: the two halves deploy as separate artifacts on separate hosts, and the site is static — there is no server side to proxy through, so the API origin has to be baked into the bundle. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Those and the local-platform gap are written down in [#28](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/issues/28) and linked from a banner on the spec. Every figure, quote and publisher in the fixtures and screenshots is invented.

I can subscribe to the PR and act on CI or review comments as they arrive — say the word and I'll wire it up.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

- session-start-hook: Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code on the web. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for Claude Code on the web, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during web sessions.
- adopt-claudinite: Bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming repo — mount, hooks, checks, skills. Use when asked to bootstrap, adopt, or set up Claudinite, or to baseline a repo to pick up updates.
- adopt-pack: Add one or more packs to an already-adopted Claudinite member — declare, run each pack's adoption interview, re-vendor, scaffold, land. Use when asked to adopt, add, enable, or declare a pack (e.g. product-wiki, executable-requirements) on a repo that already runs Claudinite.
- authoring-agent-docs: How to write instruction files coding agents follow reliably. Use before writing or editing any Claude instruction doc — a project CLAUDE.md, a convention doc, a routine spec.
- bug-investigation: Method for investigating a bug and pinning down its root cause. Use when investigating a bug report, when a fix didn't hold or a bug recurs, or when a report doesn't reproduce against main.
- ci-performance-evaluation: Method for finding where a repo's CI time actually goes and what is worth fixing. Use when CI feels slow, when investigating a runtime regression, or when the weekly ci-performance task hands you a finding.
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- extract-from-activity: Mine a window of a repo's commits, merged PRs and issue activity for durable, reusable lessons and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.
- git-github-advanced: Git/GitHub procedures beyond the baseline lifecycle. Use for commit layering, recovering a branch after a squash-merge, CI-trigger rules, GitHub Actions gotchas, or merge-relocation traps.
- github-actions-scheduling: What a GitHub Actions `schedule:` trigger actually guarantees — late fires, dropped fires, the 60-day disable — and how to build and describe scheduled work around it. Use when adding, changing, explaining, or debugging anything that runs on a cron in GitHub Actions.
- growth-dedup: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
- map-a-data-source: Reconnaissance on a website you want data from but don't control — locate the real data surface (hydration blob, client API, or markup) and write the findings down before any parser exists. Use when adding a new source to a scraper, or when an existing source stops parsing and you suspect the site changed shape.
- merge-to-main: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
- prose-to-checks: Mine pack prose (RULES.md, SKILL.md) for always-testable rules that were never converted to checks, and convert the strongest ones. Use when auditing packs for convertible rules, when the weekly prose-to-checks sweep runs, or as the upgrade pass over prose a growth-extract run just wrote.
- repo-text-sweeps: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
- single-branch-status: Assess one branch's landed status — merged, already-in-main, superseded, orphaned, or genuine unmerged work — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single branch is safe to delete, judging by content not the ref's name (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-branches task hands you branches to assess).
- single-issue-triage: Triage one open issue and take the first applicable action — close-if-implemented, needs-decision, blocked, quick-win, or leave. Use when acting on a single issue; "implemented in main" must be verified against main's current content and the default is to comment, not close (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-issues task hands you issues to triage).
- single-pr-status: Assess one open pull request's landed status — keep-open, or closeable (merged, already-in-main, superseded, stale) — read-only. Use when triaging whether a single PR should stay open, judging by its commits and diff not its title (e.g. the tidy-repo pack's tidy-prs task hands you PRs to assess).
- unattended-agents: Architecture and practices for unattended, automation-invoked agents and recurring routines. Use when building, structuring, or running an AI agent, a scheduled routine, or a multi-stage agent pipeline.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.
- writing-migration-plans: Where a plan and a design live, and how to order a plan's phases so nothing stalls mid-run — the plan is a tracking issue (never a plan document in the repo), the design doc carries only the end state with rationale and alternatives; front-load the out-of-band setup, write ALL the code including the cleanup and take one approval for the stack, then chain every execution step to the verification of the one before it as a queued continuation, and keep the tracking issue append-only while implementing. Use BEFORE writing any DESIGN.md, migration plan, phased implementation plan, rollout or cutover plan — including the moment you are about to create a docs/<initiative>/ file — and when working through a plan's tracking issue.
- writing-tasks: The contract a Claudinite task is written to — the declaration's fields, the code-work and agentic phases, the precondition as the only decision point, ordering, and how a work item converges. Use when writing or changing a tasks/<name>/task.mjs or its worker, or when a task-declaration check fires.
- writing-tests: Practices for writing tests you can trust. Use before writing or changing any test — see-it-fail discipline, snapshot/golden rules, CI-only and heavy-browser tests, fuzzy-metric gating.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". # Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
